_readme: Hand-maintained fixes for data/sources/wikidata-events.json, applied by scripts/build-data.mjs. 'exclude' drops items that aren't historical events (each with a reason). 'places' sets where an event happened (modern country code p and [lat, lon] ll) when Wikidata has no location. 'dates' overrides a start (s) or end (e) date where Wikidata has a clear typo; each entry says why. Dates use the same format as events.json: '1877-01-29', '1877' or '-0229' for 229 BC. Consider fixing the item on Wikidata too.

Q154552.why: Illyro-Roman Wars were 229–168 BC; Wikidata has the years as AD.

Q714820.why: Satsuma Rebellion began 29 January 1877; Wikidata has 2005.

Q1187198.why: Ten Tragic Days were 9–19 February 1913; Wikidata has the end as 1910.

Q137612545.why: 2025–2026 Iranian protests began in 2025, as the name says; Wikidata has 2020.

Q49097.why: The 1948 Palestine war began with civil war on 30 November 1947; Wikidata gives only the 1940s.

Q122962941.why: The Gaza War began on 7 October 2023, as its own description says; Wikidata gives only the 2020s.

Q51649.why: The First Crusade was 1096–1099; Wikidata gives the 1080s and 1098.

Q12546.why: The Crusades to the Holy Land ran from 1096 to the fall of Acre in 1291.

Q126065.why: The Iranian Revolution began with protests in 1978; Wikidata gives 1970.
